title: wc_crypto2dev_assign_devid and _ssl are 50 lines of nearly identical code
description: wc_crypto2dev_assign_devid(WOLFSSL_CTX*) and wc_crypto2dev_assign_devid_ssl(WOLFSSL*) share the same logic: save prev_safe_mode, set g_tls_safe_mode=1, register device, call SetDevId, roll back on failure. The only difference is wolfSSL_CTX_SetDevId vs wolfSSL_SetDevId. The 50-line body is duplicated with a superfluous brace block around it ({int prev_safe_mode = ...}) that does not limit scope in any meaningful way. Suggested rewrite: extract a shared static helper 'crypto2dev_assign_devid_common(int (*set_fn)(void*, int), void* obj)' and call it from both public functions.
